india-macro.title: Govt pledges extra Rs 30,000 crore for NIIF, move to spur infra investments, says finance ministry

This significant boost aims to accelerate investments in crucial sectors like transportation, energy, and digital infrastructure, fostering economic growth and job creation. The move is expected to attract further private capital, supporting India's ambition to become a developed nation by 2047 amidst global economic challenges.

The government believes that by investing in these sectors, it can help stimulate economic growth and job creation. india-macro.title: India's external debt rises to $762.8 billion in FY26, debt-to-GDP ratio climbs
india-macro.summary: India's external debt reached $762.8 billion by March 2026, a rise of $26.3 billion year-on-year, pushing the debt-to-GDP ratio to 20.8%. The US dollar's strength significantly impacted this figure. While long-term debt saw a modest increase, short-term debt's share grew, raising concerns about its proportion to foreign exchange reserves. Despite these shifts, debt servicing as a percentage of current receipts declined.
india-macro.quick_take: India's external debt rose to $762.8 billion by March 2026, reflecting rising financial concerns amidst a strong US dollar.
india-macro.simplified_article: India's external debt, which is money owed to foreign lenders, increased by $26.3 billion over the past year, reaching $762.8 billion. This rise is partly due to the US dollar becoming stronger, which makes foreign debt more expensive in local currency terms. The country's debt in relation to its economic output (debt-to-GDP ratio) is now 20.8%. Although long-term borrowing went up only slightly, there’s been a significant rise in short-term debt, raising worries about its impact on the country's foreign currency savings. Fortunately, the amount the country needs to pay back from its current income has decreased.
india-macro.investor_impact: This increase in external debt might lead to higher borrowing costs and affect sectors reliant on foreign loans, such as infrastructure and manufacturing. If you're in a business that depends on foreign funding, you could see tighter lending conditions ahead. Additionally, the rising short-term debt could impact currency values and influence investments in forex markets.

crypto.title: MiCA's looming deadline could leave 10 million crypto users without a platform in the EU
crypto.summary: As MiCA takes full effect on July 1, SwissBorg's Alex Fazel told CoinDesk users should choose platforms built to withstand EU regulators' tightening oversight.
crypto.quick_take: With MiCA regulations starting on July 1, up to 10 million crypto users in the EU may find themselves without a trading platform.
crypto.simplified_article: New laws called MiCA (Markets in Crypto-Assets) will be fully effective from July 1, affecting how crypto platforms operate in the EU. This regulation aims to tighten oversight and ensure safer trading environments. Currently, an estimated 10 million users rely on various crypto platforms, but many may not meet the new requirements. As a result, these users might lose access to their trading platforms unless they switch to compliant providers. Experts recommend choosing platforms that are ready for these changes to avoid disruption.

crypto.title: Ripple wants institutions to borrow against tokenized assets on XRPL
crypto.summary: A proposed XRPL standard would let institutions borrow against tokenized assets, with the blockchain enforcing loan terms while the underwriting stays with human credit teams. It still needs validator approval to go live.
crypto.quick_take: Ripple plans to let institutions borrow against tokenized assets on its XRPL blockchain, making loans smarter and more efficient.
crypto.simplified_article: Ripple has proposed a new standard for its XRPL (XRP Ledger), allowing institutions to secure loans backed by digital assets they own. This idea aims to streamline borrowing processes, with the blockchain automatically enforcing terms, while people will still evaluate creditworthiness. The XRPL is a platform for fast, low-cost transactions using digital tokens. The proposal needs approval from validators before it can be implemented, which could benefit banks and financial companies looking to use crypto assets for lending.
